about: Dense-path calibration (model.js predictDense, denseCal). The bench lines (bench.gpu) were fitted on plain llama-style models whose weights are K-quants, Q4_0 or Q8_0. Three things those lines do not see are measured here and turned into terms at run time: (1) kernels: a quant type whose decode kernel runs below the line (per backend and card, from kernel microbenchmarks or fitted on whole-model points); (2) layers: a non-plain layer (linear attention / Gated DeltaNet) costs time a plain layer does not; (3) KV: the read rate of the attention cache at depth. Every term names its source. points: whole-model decode measurements with the bytes each one reads per token by ggml type and layer kind (GGUF headers, READ); use = fit (sets a term), holdout (never sets one: tests the terms), line (a row the bench line itself was fitted on), context (a build or condition the planner does not model; shown, never fitted). report.js --dense-cal prints predicted vs measured for every point, without (before) and with (after) these terms.

kernels.src: homelab lab notes 'The single-stream gap' (2026-09-23): test-backend-ops perf, one token, 65,536 x 5,120 weights too large for cache, upstream 9425611 SYCL on a B70: Q4_K 581, Q5_K 585, Q6_K 590, f16 593 GB/s (= the line: ref 585), IQ4_XS 324, IQ4_NL 98 (no reorder layout; the 16-entry table lookup bounds them); IQ3_S from 'Q3_K and IQ3_S join the XMX path': one IQ3_S weight 364 us at one stream against a ~65 us read (65 / 364 x 590 = 105 GB/s). Q8_0 reads at the line on big weights (bench row odie-sycl-ha8b-q8_0-r1-0903 sits -0.34 ms off it)

ESTIMATE: no SYCL decode kernel of these grid types is measured; they decode through the same codebook-grid lookup as IQ3_S (homelab lab notes: 'the same class of cost as the IQ4 table lookup measured on the B70s'), so they borrow its rate

lab notes step 5 (chain-bench, B70 #1, every weight from DRAM, one token): a 17,408 x 5,120 PTQ1_0 weight (19.5 MB) in 88.83 us on the prism upstream MMVQ kernel (arm A-278) = 219.5 GB/s, against the Q4_K control (50.1 MB) in 87.8 us = 571 GB/s (ref). Our base-3 reorder kernel (arm B) reads it in 40.06 us (487 GB/s) but carries 15 more patches, so it stays context

terms.src: the KV read rate at depth over the line rate: the two depths of one build and file (the decode time added between them over the KV bytes added, at the line rate)

ms a linear-attention (Gated DeltaNet) layer adds to a decode step beyond its weight bytes: the measured step less host, every weight at its kernel rate and the KV, over the linear layers. The 2026-09-23 profile of the same build splits it: DeltaNet state + conv ~3.5 ms, 96 tiny Q8_0 DeltaNet projections at 21 GB/s ~1.2 ms, small elementwise ops a few ms (1,505 kernels a token against Qwen3-4B's 616)

ms per billion IQ weights on the Quadro RTX 6000 (Turing sm_75, CUDA): its IQ kernels are bound by the codebook dequantization, not the bytes, so the cost follows the weight count (GSQ IQ2_XS is 28 % smaller than IQ3_S and decodes at the same 25 tok/s). Fitted on one GSQ file, held out on the other

assumed.src: ESTIMATE: not separable on Turing (both GSQ points carry the same 48 linear layers, so any per-layer cost moves into the IQ weight term); on Ampere qwen27 UD-Q4_K_XL (48 linear layers) reads at the line within -2 % (holdout cuda-ampere-qwen27-udq4kxl-screen), so 0
ESTIMATE: no sliding-window model is measured on any of our lines; a sliding layer is costed as a plain layer that reads its window of KV, and the stated error widens
ESTIMATE: KV read at the weight-read rate where no depth pair is measured (the snoopy 3090 Ti Nanbeige depth range holds within the dense test's bounds at 1)

bpw.src: ggml type_traits: block bytes x 8 / block weights (IQ4_XS 136/256, IQ4_NL 18/32, IQ3_S 110/256, IQ3_XXS 98/256, IQ2_S 82/256, IQ2_XS 74/256, IQ2_XXS 66/256, IQ1_S 50/256, IQ1_M 56/256)

kernel_bound.src: quant types whose decode kernel can run below the bytes line (codebook / table / ternary decode): on a card with no measured rate for one, the stated error widens

free_test_cards.src: a resident service on a card marked test_card (data.boxes ... other[].test_card) is planned as stopped: the owner's standing rule is that odie's B70s are test cards and an experiment outranks a local seat's uptime (homelab lab notes odie row: both B70s serve tests since 2026-10-24). The plan names the service it displaces (prediction.displaces). knobs.freeTestCards false plans around the resident instead

unmeasured_kernel_pct.src: a kernel-bound type with no measured rate on the card: the measured ones run at 17-55 % of the line on SYCL (IQ4_NL / IQ3_S / IQ4_XS) and the Turing IQ files decode at 46-62 % of their bytes rate, so the prediction can be up to ~2x fast

unmeasured_layer_pct.src: a layer kind with no fitted cost on the card (sliding window anywhere, linear attention off SYCL): qwen27's 48 linear layers cost 16 % of its SYCL step

deep_model_pct.src: more layers than the line's models (28-36): the line's intercept holds their per-layer launch cost; SYCL runs ~17 small kernels a layer at 4-5 us each (Qwen3-4B profile, lab notes), ~0.08 ms a layer the line does not see

deep_layers.src: the most layers of a model the bench lines were fitted on (Qwen3-1.7B 28, Llama-3-8B 32, Qwen3-8B 36)

no_holdout_pct.src: a card backend with no holdout point (no dense measurement off the line's own rows): its error is the line's alone, untested on a model this size

cpu_spill_pct.src: layers on the CPU: the measured spill (snoopy Nanbeige 81,920, ~12 of 52 layers on the CPU) decoded 5.7-6.2 tok/s where the plan with the spill measured reads 8.4 at that depth

borrowed_kernel_plus.v: fastest measured kernel-bound rate on the card
borrowed_kernel_plus.src: a borrowed rate (no measurement of the type itself) can be wrong both ways: the faster side of the stated error is the step with every borrowed byte read at the fastest kernel-bound rate MEASURED on that card (SYCL: IQ4_XS 324 GB/s against the borrowed IQ3_S 105)

floor_pct.src: the least stated error: the median line residual of the plain rows (bench.gpu) is a few %, and builds move a step by 5-10 % (lab notes patch series)
